data.title: ClearPoint Neuro Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Investment
data.description:
Clearpoint Neuro, Inc. ((CLPT)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

ClearPoint Neuro’s third-quarter earnings call struck a broadly constructive tone, as revenue climbed 36% and the company reported strength across navigation, capital equipment and laboratory services. Investors also heard about a record capital-sales quarter, a broad partner pipeline and several planned 2027 milestones, although lower margins, cash usage and regulatory uncertainty remained important risks.

Revenue Growth Accelerates

ClearPoint Neuro generated $12.1 million in third-quarter revenue, up from $8.9 million a year earlier, marking 36% growth. Operating expenses rose 23% as management continued investing in infrastructure and commercial scale.

Biologics and Drug Delivery Gains

Revenue from biologics and drug delivery increased 11% to $4.9 million from $4.4 million. The improvement was primarily tied to higher service revenue performed at ClearPoint Advanced Laboratories, or CAL.

Navigation Revenue Jumps

Neurosurgery navigation revenue surged 59% to $5.4 million from $3.4 million. Management attributed the increase mainly to IRRAflow sales following the IRRAS acquisition, along with continued growth in legacy neurosurgery products.

Capital Equipment Shows Strong Demand

Capital equipment and software revenue rose 68% to $1.7 million from $1.0 million. Growth reflected higher placements of ClearPoint navigation systems, Prism laser units and IRRAflow control units.

Record Capital Sales Support Pipeline

ClearPoint reported its largest capital-sales quarter in company history, while describing its sales funnel as healthier than ever. Demand spans IRRAflow pumps, Prism systems, navigation platforms for drug-delivery trials and ICT systems for operating-room procedures.

AMT-130 Regulatory Process Advances

Partner uniQure submitted a biologics license application to the FDA for AMT-130, an investigational Huntington’s disease treatment, with ClearPoint’s device documentation on file. If the application is accepted for review, ClearPoint expects a potential companion 510(k) submission for its device.

Broad Partner and Phase III Pipeline

ClearPoint now supports more than 60 active biopharma partners, giving the company exposure to a wide range of clinical programs. Several Phase III studies are enrolling or expected to begin in 2027, with larger trials potentially involving up to 200 patients across about 20 sites.

Advanced Laboratories Continue Expanding

The company continued expanding its Torrey Pines CAL facility with additional capacity, equipment and personnel. Planned or growing capabilities include PET and SPECT tracers, radiopharmaceuticals and histology services.

Commercial Integration Improves

Management said operating performance benefited from continued IRRAS integration and a reorganization of the clinical field team ahead of Phase III trials. Sales and marketing expenses were more than 15% lower than in the second quarter of 2026.

Robotics and Focused Ultrasound Progress

ClearPoint is developing a dedicated cranial robotic platform designed to support fast, accurate, multi-trajectory procedures. It is also working on focused ultrasound technology intended to move drug delivery and blood-brain barrier disruption from MRI suites into operating rooms and infusion clinics.

Spinal Laser Program Receives Grant Support

ClearPoint became an industry partner in a five-year NCI R01 grant led by Dartmouth Health. The program will study MR-guided laser treatment for spinal metastases, progressing from laboratory work through preclinical validation and eventually a clinical trial using the Prism system.

IRRAflow Milestones Planned for 2027

ClearPoint identified five key IRRAflow milestones for 2027: launches of Shoreline software, the Dart catheter and a next-generation forward-tunneling catheter. The company also plans to present randomized ARCH trial results and pursue a specific FDA indication for subdural hematoma.

Cash Position Gains Flexibility

ClearPoint ended the quarter with $46.2 million in cash and equivalents. It also used its existing at-the-market facility for the first time, raising $22 million in net proceeds to support CAL expansion, IRRAflow integration, robotics, focused ultrasound and potential 2027 launches.

Growth Expected to Continue

Management said capital equipment, disposable products and CAL services could all support fourth-quarter growth. CAL revenue has increased sequentially for three straight quarters, while executives said they remained comfortable with a base-business growth outlook in the mid-teens for 2027, without issuing formal guidance.

Gross Margin Comes Under Pressure

Third-quarter gross margin fell to 58% from 63% a year earlier. The decline mainly reflected overhead at the new CAL facility and additional amortization from acquired intangible assets, partly offset by lower other costs of revenue.

Operating Costs Rise Across the Business

Research and development expense increased 16% to $4.0 million, driven mainly by $0.6 million in higher personnel costs. Sales and marketing expense rose 44% to $5.5 million, while general and administrative expense climbed 7% to $3.8 million.

Cash Burn and Investment Remain Key Risks

Operational cash burn totaled $20.1 million through the first nine months of 2026. Management also expects additional CAL-related capital spending over the next 12 months, although it aims to reduce quarterly operating burn gradually over the coming four to six quarters.

AMT-130 Timing Remains Uncertain

Management cautioned that the FDA could accept, reject or delay the AMT-130 application. If accepted, a potential approval was described as occurring roughly six to eight months later, assuming the process proceeds according to plan.

Spinal Laser Work Is Still Early

The spinal laser therapy program remains at an early research stage, and the Prism system is not currently cleared for spinal use. ClearPoint said the regulatory pathway and eventual label remain uncertain as work focuses on preclinical development and initial clinical-trial patients.

Mature DBS Market Offers Limited Growth

Management described MRI navigation for deep brain stimulation as a mature market with limited expected growth. ClearPoint views the business as being in a harvest stage and considers it the smallest opportunity in its broader portfolio.

CAL Services Require Upfront Investment

Some CAL services require equipment purchases and technician hiring three to six months before a study can begin. As a result, management does not expect histology revenue during the next six months while the capability is being built.

Guidance and Outlook

ClearPoint cited a $49 million midpoint for 2026 revenue and said it still sees mid-teens base-business growth in 2027, though formal 2027 guidance has not been issued. Management expects more insight and an early revenue update in the second week of January, while targeting revenue growth above operating-expense growth, additional CAL investment, several Phase III starts within 12 to 15 months and five major 2027 milestones.

Overall, ClearPoint’s call showed a company gaining commercial momentum across navigation, capital equipment and laboratory services while building a substantial clinical pipeline. The opportunity is balanced by weaker margins, meaningful cash burn, planned investment and regulatory uncertainty, making execution on 2027 milestones central to the investment case.

data.title: B2Gold Earnings Call Signals Lower Costs and Growth
data.description:
B2Gold Corp. ((TSE:BTO)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

B2Gold’s third-quarter call carried a strongly positive tone, with management highlighting solid production, lower cost guidance, improving free cash flow and ample liquidity. Challenges including Fekola’s waste-stripping phase, Goose’s ramp-up costs, higher diesel prices and hedging losses were acknowledged but presented as manageable.

Production Beats Expectations, Costs Decline

B2Gold produced more than 193,000 ounces in the third quarter and remained on track for its full-year production target. Strong year-to-date performance allowed the company to reduce consolidated all-in sustaining cost guidance by more than $100 per ounce at the midpoint, to $2,230-$2,310 per ounce sold.

Revenue Benefits From Higher Gold Prices

Quarterly revenue reached $836 million, supported by roughly 195,000 ounces of gold sales at an average realized price of $4,290 per ounce. This was the first full quarter in which sales reflected spot gold prices after prepaid gold deliveries were completed in June 2026.

Adjusted Earnings and Cash Flow Strengthen

Adjusted net income attributable to shareholders was $183 million, or $0.14 per share. Operating cash flow before working capital movements was $387 million, while cash flow after those adjustments totaled $239 million.

Free Cash Flow Turns Positive

B2Gold generated $48 million of free cash flow during the quarter, helped by stronger realized gold prices and better operating performance. Major Goose construction and ramp-up spending was largely behind the company, while prepaid gold commitments had been completed by the end of June.

Balance Sheet Provides Financial Flexibility

The company ended the quarter with $294 million in cash and cash equivalents and working capital of $497 million. It also had approximately $705 million available under its revolving credit facility, giving management room to fund operations, growth projects and shareholder returns.

Shareholder Returns Continue

B2Gold returned capital through $59 million of share repurchases during the quarter, including $33 million highlighted in management’s comments. Executives said capital allocation would remain disciplined, balancing buybacks with investment in existing mines and exploration.

Fekola Regional Moves Toward Development

B2Gold received the Menankoto exploitation permit on August 7 and began stripping activities shortly after the quarter ended. Ore production at Fekola Regional is expected to begin in early 2027, with steady-state output projected to add about 150,000 ounces annually from 2028.

Goose Crushing Upgrade Improves Throughput

The Phase 1 upgrade of Goose’s fixed crushing plant was completed shortly after quarter-end and commissioned in mid-October. Throughput was averaging about 3,200 tonnes per day, a level management said should support a much stronger fourth quarter.

Goose Phase 2 Supports Long-Term Growth

The Phase 2 upgrade at Goose remains scheduled for the second quarter of 2027. Once completed, the crusher is expected to consistently process an average of 4,000 tonnes per day, supporting the mine’s targeted annual production of 300,000 ounces.

Flexible Processing Helps Manage Goose Output

The mobile crusher remains available to provide capacity above the 3,200-tonne daily baseline. Testing showed that the mill can handle about 4,000 tonnes per day, giving Goose a working range of 3,200-4,000 tonnes to manage ore tonnes, grade and ounces.

Exploration Adds Confidence at Goose

Infill drilling increased confidence in the underground resource base at LAMA and Nuvuyak. B2Gold also announced Tatuk, a high-grade discovery on the Western Limb of the Banded Iron Formation at Portage Nuvuyak, marking the first new Goose discovery since the project was acquired.

Masbate and Otjikoto Deliver Strong Results

Masbate and Otjikoto produced another strong quarter and helped offset lower output at Fekola. Masbate cash cost guidance fell to $800-$900 per ounce, while all-in sustaining cost guidance declined to $1,250-$1,400; Otjikoto’s all-in sustaining cost range was reduced by $200 to $1,630-$1,780 per ounce.

Fekola Cost Guidance Falls

Fekola’s all-in sustaining cost guidance was reduced to $2,350-$2,500 per ounce sold from $2,670-$2,820 previously. Management attributed most of the reduction to lower royalties resulting from a gold price assumption below the one used when the original guidance was established.

Fekola Underground Reaches Full Ramp-Up

Fekola’s underground operation was described as fully ramped up, operating at roughly 4,000 tonnes per day with grades of about 3-3.5 grams per tonne. Management called the underground the project’s current highlight because its grades are higher than those of the open pit.

Several Growth Catalysts Build Into 2027

Management pointed to multiple potential growth drivers, including Fekola Regional’s early contribution, Goose’s midyear Phase 2 upgrade and continued work at Antelope following Otjikoto. Exploration aimed at extending Masbate’s mine life will also be assessed using higher gold price assumptions.

Hedging Constraints Ease Next Year

The remaining gold collar contracts are scheduled to roll off in January 2027. After that point, B2Gold expects to be free of both gold prepaid commitments and gold collar contracts throughout 2027, giving it greater exposure to prevailing gold prices.

Goose Expected to Have Limited Near-Term Cash Taxes

Using a $4,000 gold price assumption, management said Goose would not be expected to pay cash taxes for roughly five years while it uses its accumulated losses. Preliminary expectations were that 2027 cash taxes could be slightly below the current year and likely below $600 million including withholding taxes.

Gramalote Work Continues

B2Gold is modifying permits, reducing risks at Gramalote and completing resettlement activities. Resettlement is expected to continue into mid- or late 2027, after which management plans to revisit a construction decision or determine the project’s next steps.

Fekola Open-Pit Output Faces Temporary Pressure

Fekola produced approximately 78,000 ounces in the quarter as open-pit activity shifted from ore mining to the Phase 8 waste-stripping campaign. The stripping work is expected to continue through the rest of 2026 and for most of 2027, weighing on near-term open-pit production.

Lower-Grade Feed During Fekola Stripping

Management expects fourth-quarter open-pit grades to be similar to the third quarter, with roughly 1.2 grams per tonne referenced for the period. During Phase 8 stripping, the mill will rely mainly on low-grade stockpiles, with initial underground feed and later Fekola Regional ore providing additional support.

Goose Production Was Constrained

Goose produced approximately 40,000 ounces during the quarter while repairs and upgrades continued on its fixed crushing circuit. All-in sustaining costs were also affected by about 10,000 ounces produced but not sold by quarter-end.

One-Time Goose Costs Lifted Quarterly Expenses

Goose’s quarterly all-in sustaining cost included about $29 million tied to the mobile crusher purchase and fire remediation. Those costs comprised roughly $12 million for the mobile crusher and $17 million for fire-related work; excluding them and the unsold ounces, normalized costs would have been closer to the upper end of the annual range.

Phase 2 Shutdown Will Require Planning

The Phase 2 fixed-crusher upgrade planned for the second quarter of 2027 will involve a 10-week shutdown. B2Gold plans to use stockpiled crushed ore and the mobile crusher during the outage, with about 3,200 tonnes per day considered a reasonable modeling assumption for that quarter.

Higher Diesel Prices Affect Goose Costs

Diesel purchased for Goose in the third quarter was significantly more expensive than a year earlier. The cost of buying and shipping fuel was about 50%-60% higher based on global prices, although the impact was partly reduced because the site used less fuel than originally expected.

Gold Collar Losses Reduce Adjusted Earnings

Adjusted net income was reduced by $47 million in realized losses on gold collar contracts during the quarter. Management said adjusted earnings would have been materially higher without those hedging-related losses.

Full-Year Guidance Remains Intact

Management expects full-year results to remain within existing guidance ranges, with consolidated all-in sustaining costs of $2,230-$2,310 per ounce sold. Masbate, Otjikoto and Fekola cost guidance stands at $800-$900 in cash costs and $1,250-$1,400 in all-in sustaining costs, $1,630-$1,780 in all-in sustaining costs, and $2,350-$2,500 in all-in sustaining costs, respectively.

Growth Outlook Centers on Goose and Fekola Regional

Goose throughput is averaging about 3,200 tonnes per day, with Phase 2 upgrades on track for the second quarter of 2027 and a longer-term target of 4,000 tonnes per day. Fekola Regional is expected to begin producing ore in early 2027, contribute roughly half of its eventual annual output during the ramp-up year and reach about 150,000 ounces annually from 2028.

B2Gold’s call combined strong financial performance with a clear pipeline of operational improvements and growth projects. While Fekola’s stripping campaign and Goose’s ramp-up create near-term pressure, lower costs, stronger cash generation, solid liquidity and advancing projects support an optimistic investment case.

data.title: Etsy Earnings Call: Growth, AI and Stronger Returns
data.description:
Etsy Inc ((ETSY)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Etsy’s earnings call carried a strongly constructive tone, with accelerating marketplace growth, rising revenue and EBITDA, improving buyer and seller trends, and stronger cash generation. Management acknowledged softer purchase frequency, tougher holiday comparisons, currency pressure and leadership changes, but the positive developments clearly outweighed the challenges.

Marketplace Growth Accelerated

Etsy marketplace gross merchandise sales reached $2.6 billion in the third quarter, up 8.8% from a year earlier. Management said this was the third consecutive quarter of accelerating growth, signaling that the marketplace has moved firmly back into expansion mode.

Revenue and Profitability Strengthened

Revenue rose 10.9% year over year to $692 million, led by 9.1% growth in marketplace revenue and 15% growth in services revenue. Adjusted EBITDA increased 14.6% to $210 million, producing a 30.4% margin and growing faster than revenue for a second straight quarter.

Active Buyers Returned to Growth

Trailing 12-month active buyers increased 1% year over year to about 88 million, marking their first annual growth in two years. The buyer base also expanded by approximately 540,000 from the second quarter, providing a stronger foundation for marketplace activity.

Acquisition and Reactivation Improved

Gross buyer additions grew 6.2% year over year in the third quarter, supported by both new customer acquisition and the reactivation of previous buyers. Social media helped bring back former customers, while spending on younger audiences, including TikTok, supported new-buyer growth.

GMS per Buyer Continued Rising

Trailing 12-month GMS per buyer climbed 3.9% year over year, extending its growth streak to three quarters. Etsy credited personalization, more relevant search, stronger quality signals, improved matching of products to buyer intent and a greater focus on special occasions.

Seller Growth and Engagement Strengthened

Etsy’s active seller base grew at its fastest pace in two years, with retention also improving. Seller growth and higher GMS per seller reflected the increasing value of better tools, support, trust and safety measures, and more data-driven seller experiences.

Personalization Became a Meaningful Growth Driver

Etsy estimated that personalization improvements contributed about two percentage points to its annualized year-over-year GMS growth rate by the third quarter. The company is extending lessons learned from its app across the web and other parts of the shopping experience.

Search and Inventory Relevance Improved

The company said its search and discovery efforts are bringing higher-quality, more relevant inventory to shoppers. Richer buyer profiles, improved ranking models and stronger quality signals are helping Etsy better distinguish between physical and digital products based on customer intent.

Advertising Efficiency Increased

Etsy’s take rate rose 50 basis points year over year to 26.2%, mainly because of improvements to Etsy Ads and, to a lesser extent, Offsite Ads. Better ad relevance, click-through rates, conversion and budget pacing helped sellers target more valuable opportunities, while marketing ROI improved.

Marketing Reached Younger Audiences

Paid social activity expanded across TikTok, YouTube and other channels, helping Etsy reach younger and new buyers. About half of TikTok impressions reached people aged 18 to 29, while an Olivia Rodrigo real-world campaign generated approximately 90 million views.

Buyer and Seller Tools Expanded

Etsy continued investing in listing creation, product customization, shared shop access, financial insights, appeals and ad management. An AI-powered seller assistant entered beta, while buyer initiatives included loyalty testing, expanded premium support for top customers and broader general support.

Human Connection Built Trust

Testing on Android and related research showed that seller stories, creative processes, craftsmanship details and seller information can improve buyer trust and perceived value. Etsy is expanding these features across platforms as it seeks to make the marketplace feel more personal and credible.

AI Shopping and Seller Tools Advanced

Etsy’s Gifting Assistant offered an early shopping-agent experience by helping customers narrow broad and complex searches. The company is also applying artificial intelligence and machine learning to personalization, discovery, seller insights and shop management.

Gifting Remained Central to Demand

Approximately 30% of Etsy’s GMS comes from gifting, making occasions an important source of customer activity. Home and living, jewelry and vintage were strong categories, while weddings, back-to-school and Halloween also performed well across a broad range of markets and income groups.

Cash Generation and Liquidity Improved

Etsy held $2.5 billion in cash equivalents and short- and long-term investments as of September 30, 2026, including proceeds from the Depop sale. Operating cash flow from continuing operations reached $243 million, and free cash flow conversion equaled 112% of adjusted EBITDA.

Debt Reduction and Buybacks Accelerated

On October 1, Etsy paid $649 million to settle the remaining principal on its 2019 Notes. The company also repurchased about $395 million of stock during the quarter, reducing its share count by roughly 5.2 million shares, while retaining $2.2 billion in authorized repurchase capacity.

AI Listing Rules Reinforced Differentiation

Etsy clarified that sellers must provide at least one unaltered photo of an item with a real background and cannot use AI-generated functional guides such as patterns or recipes. The company is strengthening enforcement and said the policy changes should not materially affect near-term GMS.

Momentum Was Broad Across Customers

Management reported spending growth across all household-income groups, although gains were relatively stronger among higher-income customers. Repeat and habitual buyers increased for consecutive quarters, while Etsy’s most valuable buyers grew sequentially for the second quarter in a row.

Purchase Frequency Remained a Weak Spot

Overall purchase frequency was still modestly lower than a year earlier, despite improving engagement indicators and sequential gains among repeat and habitual buyers. Management said the company has not yet returned to year-over-year growth in total frequency, leaving customer activity as an important area to improve.

Leadership Transitions Are Approaching

CFO Lanny Baker is scheduled to leave Etsy in early March, and the company has started searching for a Brooklyn-based successor. Investor relations leader Deb Wasser also participated in her final earnings call before retirement, with Sarah Marx expected to take over the function.

Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year Guidance

For the fourth quarter, Etsy expects marketplace GMS of $3.46 billion to $3.52 billion, representing approximately 5% to 7% year-over-year growth, with a take rate near 25.6% and an adjusted EBITDA margin near 30%. For the full year, management expects GMS growth of about 7%, a take rate near 25.8% and an adjusted EBITDA margin of roughly 30%, assuming stable macroeconomic conditions, modest currency pressure and tougher comparisons.

Etsy’s earnings call showed a marketplace gaining momentum through better discovery, personalization, marketing efficiency and customer engagement. While softer purchase frequency, holiday uncertainty, currency headwinds and executive changes remain risks, accelerating GMS, stronger profitability, healthy cash flow and shareholder returns leave the company’s overall outlook notably constructive.

data.title: Viavi Solutions Earnings Call Signals Strong Growth Ahead
data.description:
Viavi Solutions Inc ((VIAV)) has held its Q1 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Viavi Solutions delivered a strongly positive fiscal first-quarter performance, beating revenue, margin and earnings guidance while benefiting from powerful data-center and aerospace demand. Weak wireless spending, seasonally softer OSP revenue ahead and lower cash balances were the main concerns, but management raised its near-term growth outlook.

Revenue Beat Expectations

Viavi reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $469.3 million, above its $450 million to $460 million target. Revenue rose 5.9% sequentially and 56.9% from a year earlier, reflecting broad strength across key markets.

Margins and EPS Outperformed

Operating margin reached 29%, ahead of the 26.7% to 27.5% forecast and up sharply from both prior periods. Earnings per share came in at $0.47, exceeding guidance of $0.40 to $0.42 and increasing $0.32 year over year.

Tariff Refund Added to Results

A tariff refund provided an approximately 110-basis-point boost to operating margin and added about $0.02 to EPS. Those benefits were partly offset by an additional week of certain variable expenses, making the quarter’s underlying performance important to investors.

NSC Revenue Surged

NSC revenue climbed 74.1% year over year to $376.1 million, beating guidance of $360 million to $368 million. Demand for lab, production and field products was supported by data-center expansion, the Spirent product lines and strong aerospace and defense activity.

NSC Margins Expanded

NSC gross margin rose 310 basis points year over year to 66.2%, helped by the tariff refund and a favorable product mix. Operating margin expanded to 25.5% from 8.2%, exceeding guidance as higher revenue produced stronger operating leverage.

OSP Delivered Growth

OSP revenue increased 12.2% year over year to $93 million, above its $90 million to $92 million target. Growth came from 3D sensing, anti-counterfeiting and other products, while operating margin reached 43.2%, up six percentage points from a year earlier.

Cash Flow Improved

Operating cash flow more than tripled to $104.7 million from $31 million in the comparable period. Management attributed the improvement to higher net income and the timing of working-capital movements.

Buybacks Expanded

Viavi repurchased about 3.95 million shares for approximately $150 million, at an average price of $37.98. With roughly $18 million remaining under the existing authorization, the board approved a new $500 million plan, while keeping organic investment and potential acquisitions as capital-allocation priorities.

Data-Center Demand Stayed Strong

Management said data-center demand continued to drive strong sales of instruments used in scale-up, scale-out and scale-across deployments. The company also expects robust growth in this market in calendar 2027, supported by expanding infrastructure needs.

Semiconductor Market Opens

Viavi has expanded its addressable market into semiconductor packaging and testing through NPO and CPO technologies. Initial shipments began in the September quarter, and management said the opportunity could grow into a business worth more than $100 million annually within a couple of years.

Fiber Opportunities Broaden

The company identified additional opportunities in fiber-optic and connector manufacturing as fiber densification, multicore fiber, massive parallel connectors and integrated silicon photonics develop. These markets add to Viavi’s established testing activity for pluggable optical modules.

Aerospace and Defense Momentum Continued

Aerospace and defense produced another quarter of strong sequential and year-over-year growth. Demand covered positioning, navigation, timing, communications and avionics, along with systems for drones, anti-spoofing, jamming and resilient navigation across air, land and maritime applications.

Army Selection Adds Potential

Viavi’s TRx system was selected by the U.S. Army’s Threat Systems Management Office to create realistic electromagnetic environments at newly opened test ranges. The platform will support drone, counter-drone and interceptor development, creating what management described as a potentially sizable multiyear opportunity.

Service-Provider Demand Beat Seasonality

The service-provider business performed better than seasonal expectations, with increased demand for fiber-monitoring systems used in network build-outs. Cable instruments supporting DOCSIS 4.0 and distributed access architecture also contributed to the improvement.

Refresh Cycle May Be Starting

Management reported early signs of a multiyear service-provider equipment refresh cycle. Customers are beginning to upgrade or replace equipment purchased between 2020 and 2022, which could create a broader source of demand if the trend develops.

CPO and OCS Testing Expand

Initial semiconductor packaging and testing shipments are primarily supporting co-packaged optics, or CPO. Management sees higher volume in CPO linked to switches and ASICs, while optical circuit switching may offer lower volume but greater value per shipment and particularly attractive testing content per port.

1.6T Cycle Is Still Early

The 1.6-terabit optical-module cycle remains in its early stages, while 800-gigabit products continue to represent the largest shipment category. Both generations are expected to operate in parallel for some time, with 1.6T not expected to overtake 800G before the end of calendar 2027.

Spirent Integration Progressed

Management said the operational integration of Spirent was completed two to three quarters ago and that current NSC margins now reflect business scale rather than remaining integration synergies. Product-line integration is about 25% complete, with more than 75% expected by the end of next calendar year.

Operating Leverage Supported Profit

Viavi cited significant operating leverage as revenue rises, with quarterly incremental fall-through in the high-50s to low-60s percentage range. Management offered the low- to mid-50s as a more conservative planning assumption, while an 8% effective tax rate also supported profitability.

Wireless Remained a Weak Spot

Wireless products were the main lowlight in the service-provider business because customer spending remains anemic. Management said wireless has been a headwind for three years, although it remains constructive about longer-term prospects tied to AI-RAN and 6G development.

Cash Balance Declined

Cash and short-term investments fell to $535.3 million at the end of the first quarter from $656.7 million at the end of fiscal 2026’s fourth quarter. The decline occurred alongside substantial share repurchases and other uses of capital.

Second-Quarter Outlook Raised

For fiscal second quarter 2027, Viavi expects revenue of $505 million to $515 million, NSC revenue of $426 million to $434 million and OSP revenue of $79 million to $81 million. Operating margin is forecast at 29.3%, plus or minus 30 basis points, with EPS of $0.50 to $0.52.

Growth Guidance Points Higher

Management expects quarter-over-quarter growth to continue through the rest of the fiscal year, with strong NSC demand more than offsetting weaker seasonal OSP revenue. It also expects to reach a $2 billion annualized revenue run rate during the second quarter and sees momentum continuing into the second half.

Longer-Term Growth Drivers

Viavi expects strong data-center and aerospace and defense momentum to continue into calendar 2027. Management also sees semiconductor packaging and testing becoming a major growth area, potentially exceeding $100 million for the company within a couple of years.

Overall, Viavi’s earnings call showed strong execution, expanding margins and accelerating demand in data centers, aerospace and defense and emerging optical markets. Seasonal OSP weakness, wireless softness and lower cash were notable risks, but the higher outlook and new growth opportunities gave the quarter an optimistic tone.

data.title: Fiera Capital Earnings Call Highlights Debt and Outflows
data.description:
Fiera Capital A ((TSE:FSZ)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Fiera Capital’s earnings call struck a largely negative tone despite signs of progress. Lower expenses, debt repayment, stronger recent Canadian equity results and resilient existing-client demand were outweighed by major AUM outflows, weaker revenue and performance fees, lower year-over-year EBITDA, elevated leverage and the end of the quarterly dividend.

Balance Sheet Deleveraging

Net debt ended the quarter at $689 million, down $34 million sequentially, as Fiera used stronger free cash flow to repay its credit facility. The funded debt ratio improved to 3.1x from 3.3x in the prior quarter.

More Capacity for Debt Reduction

Management said ending the quarterly dividend will create more than $45 million a year for debt reduction. The retained capital should also support reinvestment in the business and selected growth opportunities.

Broader Investment Platform

Fiera is adding core and quantitative investment strategies to expand the solutions available to clients. Management said the expansion is intended to preserve the firm’s high-conviction investment approach while broadening product choice.

Canadian Equity Team Rebuilt

The Canadian large-cap equity team added three hires with a combined 68 years of experience, including Charles Nadim as head of Canadian equities. Fiera has engaged consultants and clients, retained all but one consultant rating and reported no identified additional outflow pipeline.

Canadian Equity Performance Rebounds

The Canadian Equity Fund gained almost seven percentage points against its index in six weeks, while Canadian Equity Core was about six points ahead year to date. In October, Canadian equity strategies outperformed their benchmark by more than 500 basis points, recovering much of their earlier shortfall.

Wider Equity Momentum

Most flagship equity strategies beat their benchmarks in October, with other Canadian, U.S. and international strategies outperforming by more than 300 basis points. U.S. large-cap growth and U.S. SMID-cap growth ranked in the first or second quartile, while Atlas Group and Frontier markets also added value.

More Stable Sub-Advised Base

Sub-advised assets now represent 16% of total AUM, down from 27% two years ago. Less than one-quarter of the remaining assets are tied to clients with mandates above $1 billion, and management described the base as more stable and largely multi-strategy.

Private Markets Deployment

Fiera deployed nearly $400 million into new private-market projects during the quarter, taking year-to-date deployment to $1.2 billion. Undeployed capital in the pipeline remained substantial at $1.6 billion.

Private Markets Deliver Positive Returns

All private-market strategies generated positive absolute returns during the quarter. Since inception, core and small-cap industrial real estate strategies produced annualized returns of 8% and 13%, while the Direct Lending Opportunities Fund generated a 2.4% quarterly internal rate of return and 12% since inception.

Private Credit Becomes a Priority

Management identified private credit as an important growth area and strategic initiative. Fiera appointed Amit Gupta as global head of real estate debt and added a head of private credit to give the business greater leadership focus.

Strong Demand from Existing Canadian Clients

Core Canadian gross sales totaled $2.1 billion, including about $200 million of new mandates and a $1.9 billion positive net contribution from existing clients. Gross sales were broadly consistent with the previous two quarters.

Fixed Income Holds Long-Term Advantage

Canadian fixed-income strategies had a difficult quarter but finished close to their benchmarks. About 78% of fixed-income AUM outperformed over one year, while 94% outperformed over three years.

Sequential Expense Improvement

SG&A and other expenses excluding share-based compensation fell to $107.4 million, down $5.7 million, or 5%, from the prior quarter. Lower compensation costs led the decline, with travel, marketing and sub-advisory expenses also moving lower.

Cost Savings Build Through the Year

Year-to-date SG&A excluding share-based compensation declined $22.4 million, or 6%. About 70% of the reduction came from lower compensation costs tied to optimization efforts, with the remainder mainly reflecting lower sub-advisory fees.

Adjusted EBITDA Improves Sequentially

Adjusted EBITDA rose to $42.9 million, up $900,000, or 2.1%, from the prior quarter. The adjusted EBITDA margin increased to 28.5% from 27.1%, a 140-basis-point improvement.

Quarterly Net Earnings Increase

Net earnings attributable to shareholders rose to $6.7 million, or $0.06 per basic and diluted share. That compared with $3.5 million, or $0.03 per share, in the prior quarter.

Free Cash Flow Remains Resilient

Last-12-month free cash flow was $90 million, down $3 million sequentially but up $3 million from the same period last year. Lower lease payments and interest expense helped offset higher dividends paid to noncontrolling interests.

Directly Managed Fees Hold Steady

Base management fees from directly managed mandates were broadly unchanged from the previous quarter and flat year over year. Adjusted basic earnings per share also remained unchanged year over year at $0.23.

Operations and Technology Upgrade

Fiera continues to optimize operations, replace legacy platforms and develop artificial intelligence initiatives. The company said these efforts are designed to improve efficiency and employee productivity.

Distribution and Talent Focus

Fiera appointed Emerson Savage as head of U.S. distribution and co-head of distribution in Canada. The company is concentrating distribution resources on markets and strategies with the strongest demand, while increasing engagement with existing clients and seeking investment talent.

AUM Falls on Outflows and Markets

Total assets under management ended the quarter at $151.4 billion, down 7.4% sequentially. The decline reflected $8.3 billion of net outflows and a $3.5 billion adverse market impact, largely caused by rising rates in fixed income.

Public Markets Face Heavy Pressure

Public-markets AUM fell 8.4%, including $5.2 billion of sub-advised outflows and $2.5 billion from directly managed assets. The directly managed decline was concentrated in Canadian large-cap equity mandates.

Sub-Advised Mandates Lose Assets

Sub-advised net outflows of $5.2 billion included $3 billion of client rebalancing in the U.S. and Asia and $2.2 billion of lost mandates. About $1.5 billion of the lost mandates had been announced previously and transferred directly to PineStone.

Canadian Large-Cap Attrition Concentrated in Newer Accounts

Canadian large-cap outflows were concentrated among newer relationships, with about half of the attrition coming from clients whose average strategy tenure was 1.5 years. The business retained $15 billion of AUM, and more than 85% was held by clients with relationships exceeding five years.

Private Markets AUM Also Declines

Private-markets AUM decreased about $400 million, or 1.8%. Nearly $200 million of new mandates was more than offset by returned capital and the loss of $300 million of undeployed capital after a client chose to manage a U.K. real estate mandate internally.

Revenue Moves Lower

Third-quarter revenue was $150 million, down 3% from the prior quarter and 10% from the same quarter last year. Year-to-date revenue fell 7%, mainly because of lower sub-advised base fees, weaker performance fees and a lower share of joint-venture and associate earnings.

Performance Fees Contract Sharply

Performance fees were $600,000, compared with $2.1 million in the prior quarter and $7 million a year earlier. Year-to-date performance fees totaled $2.7 million, down from $9.7 million, with most of the decline linked to the Global Agriculture Fund.

Public-Market Base Fees Decline

Public-markets base management fees fell 5% sequentially to $91 million. They were down 11% year over year and 7% year to date, reflecting lower average AUM, reduced fee rates and a shift toward sub-advised strategies.

Commitment and Transaction Fees Fall

Commitment and transaction fees were $3.1 million, down from $3.7 million in the prior quarter. Year-to-date fees reached $8.1 million, compared with $9.7 million in the prior-year period.

Joint-Venture Earnings Weaken

Year-to-date earnings from joint ventures and associates declined to $3.7 million from $6 million a year earlier. Quarterly earnings were $2.6 million, although that represented a $200,000 sequential increase.

EBITDA Down Year Over Year

Adjusted EBITDA declined $7.4 million, or 15%, from the same quarter last year. Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA was $127.7 million, down from $139.4 million, with lower performance fees accounting for about five percentage points of the reduction.

Adjusted Earnings Per Share Declines

Adjusted net earnings fell $1.1 million year over year to $23.9 million. Fully diluted adjusted earnings per share declined to $0.19 from $0.23 a year earlier, partly reflecting dilution from the 7.4% hybrid debentures issued in May 2026.

Leverage Remains Elevated

The net debt ratio stayed at 3.8x because lower net debt was offset by lower last-12-month adjusted EBITDA. The ratio was up 0.3x from the third quarter last year, while the funded debt ratio rose to 3.1x from 2.9x.

Quarterly Dividend Discontinued

Management recommended, and the Board approved, ending the quarterly dividend. The decision is intended to retain capital, reduce leverage and improve balance-sheet flexibility, but it also removes an important source of shareholder income.

Equity Markets Remain Challenging

Quality-focused equity strategies faced elevated volatility and narrow market leadership during the quarter. Gains were concentrated in commodity-linked shares and mega-cap technology companies, producing mixed absolute and relative results across Fiera’s equity platform.

Canadian Equity Hit by Materials Underweight

Canadian equity performance was hurt by Fiera’s underweight position in materials. Gold and silver miners rallied during the period, creating a headwind for the firm’s relative returns.

Fixed Income Faces Rate Volatility

Fixed-income results were pressured by rising interest rates and uncertainty over central-bank policy. Despite the difficult quarter, longer-term relative performance remained positive across the Canadian fixed-income platform.

New-Client Sales Under Pressure

Fiera reported near-term pressure on new-client sales, especially outside Canada. The company is adjusting its local presence and distribution resources toward markets and strategies where demand is strongest.

Limited Visibility on Performance Fees

Management declined to provide fourth-quarter performance-fee guidance because markets have been volatile. Executives pointed to the sharp market movements of the previous 60 days as a reason for limited visibility.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Debt reduction is management’s first priority, with the dividend change expected to provide more than $45 million a year for repayment and another meaningful reduction by this time next year. The current expense run rate is considered a reasonable basis for the fourth quarter, while performance fees remain unpredictable and direct transfers in 2026 are expected to be lower than in 2025.

Fiera also said it does not expect the same level of leakage to PineStone and sees less of an outflow pipeline in sub-advised strategies. Management reported no additional Canadian-equity outflow pipeline, while cost optimization remains an ongoing effort.

Fiera Capital delivered some encouraging operational gains, including lower expenses, better recent equity performance and continued private-markets activity. However, the quarter was defined by shrinking AUM, falling revenue and EBITDA, high leverage and a suspended dividend, leaving investors focused on whether debt reduction and business investments can restore durable growth.

data.description:
Dexterra Group Inc. ((TSE:DXT)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Dexterra Group delivered a strongly positive quarterly update, combining record annual adjusted EBITDA and revenue with higher margins, robust free cash flow and lower leverage. Management also highlighted progress across its Canadian and U.S. growth plans, although low wildfire activity, project-timing delays and uncertainty around major awards created some near-term challenges.

Record Quarter Supports Strong Annual Performance

Dexterra reported revenue of CAD 291 million in the quarter, up from CAD 281 million a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to CAD 38 million. The adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 13% from 12.5%, and adjusted earnings per share increased 12% to CAD 0.28 as management described the period as traditionally its strongest quarter.

Growth Broad-Based Despite Wildfire Weakness

Revenue growth came from strong workforce accommodation occupancy, rental activity, organic gains and the Right Choice acquisition. Those gains offset significantly lower wildfire support and workforce accommodation installation and demobilization activity compared with last year, when those services provided a larger contribution.

Market Value Reaches a New Milestone

Dexterra surpassed CAD 1 billion in market capitalization for the first time in its history. Management linked the milestone to progress in facilities management, workforce accommodations and strategic acquisitions, supported by disciplined capital allocation and consistent financial performance.

Support Services Deliver Margin Expansion

Support Services revenue increased 8% to CAD 253 million, driven by workforce accommodation occupancy, U.S. facilities management growth and the Right Choice acquisition. Organic growth reached 4.5%, adjusted EBITDA climbed 18% to CAD 29 million, and the margin expanded to 11.5% from 10.5%, with both major platforms recording mid-single-digit organic growth.

Occupancy and Inflation Management Lift Profitability

Higher-margin workforce accommodation contracts helped improve Support Services profitability, with the margin excluding PVC rising to 11% from 10%. Management said supply-chain initiatives, contractual inflation provisions and pricing adjustments were containing cost pressures, while direct costs represented a smaller share of revenue in both segments.

PVC Investment Advances Its Platform

Dexterra’s 40% PVC investment contributed CAD 1.3 million to adjusted EBITDA, up from CAD 0.9 million a year earlier. The partnership is modernizing its proprietary PVC Connect facility-management software on time and on budget, while building the structure needed to support PVC’s distributed U.S. model.

Asset-Based Services Improve Mix

Asset Based Services generated CAD 39 million in revenue, with higher-margin rental revenue rising 2.3% on strong equipment utilization, solid access matting activity and the Right Choice contribution. Adjusted EBITDA was CAD 16 million, but the margin increased sharply to 41% from 34% because of the favorable shift toward rental revenue.

Cash Flow and Leverage Strengthen

Dexterra generated CAD 38 million of free cash flow in the quarter and CAD 61 million year to date, helped by profitability and improved working capital. Net debt fell to CAD 193 million from CAD 206 million in the second quarter, while net debt to adjusted EBITDA improved to 1.4 times from 1.6 times at the end of 2025.

Returns and Capital Discipline Remain in Focus

Trailing 12-month return on equity reached 15.4%, exceeding Dexterra’s 15% target. The company spent CAD 15 million on capital expenditures, including CAD 12 million to refurbish about 500 workforce accommodation beds, an investment management described as targeted, cost-effective and capable of generating attractive returns.

Liquidity Supports Growth and Shareholder Returns

Dexterra’s CAD 425 million credit facility runs to 2029 and has significant unused capacity, along with an uncommitted CAD 150 million accordion. The company repurchased about 118,000 shares during the quarter under its normal course issuer bid, which permits purchases of up to 3 million shares, and declared a CAD 0.10 per-share dividend payable January 15, 2027.

Pipeline Spans Canada and the United States

Management described the sales pipeline as strong and diverse across mining, energy, infrastructure, government, defense, workforce accommodations and remote facilities management. Dexterra has strengthened its U.S. leadership and sales organization supporting PVC, CMI and self-perform integrated facilities management, with new project traction in both Canada and the U.S.

New Contracts and Indigenous Partnerships Expand Reach

The company secured new facilities-management and integrated facilities-management wins in 2026, including contracts within PVC. Dexterra is also pursuing nation-building opportunities in areas such as pipelines, power, roads, defense and data centers, drawing on more than 80 Indigenous community partnerships and its national operating presence.

Fleet Expansion Targets Remote Demand

Dexterra has about 2,500 fleet beds available for medium-term deployment and is pursuing another 1,500 beds. Together, those additions would increase deployable capacity by 4,000 beds and raise total fleet capacity to 14,000, with acquisitions expected to be supported by the company’s Grande Prairie refurbishment facility.

Pricing and Data Center Opportunities Develop

Management reported positive pricing trends in elastic segments such as open camps, turnkey projects and equipment rental, with pricing gains already appearing in bids and contracts. Dexterra is also pursuing workforce accommodation opportunities in Louisiana and West Texas, Canadian data center projects and facilities-management work at an operating U.S. data center.

Near-Term Risks Include Wildfires and Project Timing

Wildfire support activity was roughly half, or slightly less than, a typical year and well below the company’s nominal CAD 25 million target. Installation and demobilization revenue declined CAD 10 million year over year because of project timing, while nation-building awards remain dependent on planning, regulatory reviews and client procurement decisions.

Management Notes Further Uncertainty

Dexterra expects PVC to be largely cash-flow neutral in the near term as it funds software modernization and builds its U.S. operating structure. Management also said the scale of future data center services remains unclear, while wildfire activity in 2027 could range from below normal to materially higher, making the outlook for those activities variable.

Forward Guidance Points to Continued Expansion

Management expects Support Services adjusted EBITDA margins to remain above 9% over the medium term, while Asset Based Services margins should be toward the upper end of the 30% to 40% range in 2026. Dexterra expects most annual free cash flow in the second half of 2026, conversion above 50%, leverage below 2.5 times, new contracts ramping through the first half of 2027 and more installation activity during 2027.

The call presented Dexterra as a growing, cash-generative company with improving margins, stronger returns and a healthier balance sheet. While wildfire volatility and the timing of major projects remain risks, management’s expanding fleet, broad pipeline and U.S. platform provide several avenues for future growth.

data.title: Innovative Industrial Properties Posts Gains, Expands Life Science Reach
data.description:
Innovative Industrial Properties ((IIPR)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Innovative Industrial Properties delivered a broadly positive third-quarter earnings call, led by stronger AFFO, record leasing activity and growing life science investments. Management also highlighted solid liquidity and conservative leverage, although operator financial stress, vacancy, re-leasing delays and uncertainty over cannabis reform remained important risks.

AFFO and Revenue Growth

Third-quarter revenue rose to $64.9 million from $63.3 million in the second quarter. AFFO increased 7% sequentially to $54.8 million, or $1.96 per diluted share, helped by new leases and the recovery of past-due rents, including a $0.15-per-share contribution from Battle Green.

Life Science Investment Expansion

The company closed $275 million of new life science commitments during the quarter. The transactions included an additional $30 million IQHQ preferred equity investment and a $245 million mezzanine loan commitment for Alewife Park, bringing total IQHQ-related commitments to about $545 million.

Alewife Park Loan Economics

The $245 million Alewife Park mezzanine loan is expected to generate an average interest rate of approximately 15.8% over its term. About $111 million was funded at closing, with the remaining $134 million expected to be funded through the fourth quarter of 2027.

Alewife Park Asset Quality and Leasing

Alewife Park is a 27-acre Cambridge, Massachusetts, campus with three buildings totaling 392,000 square feet and two pad-ready sites. The existing buildings are 78% leased to Lila Sciences, while the financing will support tenant improvements, leasing and stabilization.

Greater Portfolio Diversification

Once fully funded, life science investments are projected to represent about 26% of total annualized income. Management said the expansion improves access to lenders and capital sources while reducing the company’s dependence on a cannabis-only portfolio.

Record Quarterly Leasing Activity

The company executed new leases covering approximately 604,000 square feet across six properties during the third quarter. A further 270,000-square-foot lease signed after quarter end lifted total leasing activity since the start of the quarter to about 874,000 square feet.

Year-to-Date Leasing Momentum

Gross leasing activity reached approximately 1.3 million square feet across 12 properties during the first nine months of the year. That represents about 15% of the portfolio, and management said tenant interest remains strong with additional transactions in the pipeline.

Additional Leasing Pipeline

Agreements cover three Colorado properties totaling 72,000 square feet, subject to license transfers and regulatory approvals. Separate agreements for three properties previously leased to 4Front Ventures cover 374,000 square feet, creating a combined potential pipeline of 446,000 square feet beyond executed leases.

Improving Life Science Demand

JLL reported that combined demand in Boston, San Diego, the Bay Area and Raleigh-Durham increased 44% year over year to nearly 8 million square feet in the first quarter of 2026. The improvement was attributed to better biotech funding conditions and the reshoring of biomanufacturing.

Preferred Equity Capital

After the quarter ended, Innovative Industrial Properties completed a public offering of 2.2 million shares of 9.25% Series B preferred stock at $25 per share. The offering generated $54 million in gross proceeds, intended partly to fund the remaining Alewife Park commitment.

Liquidity and Leverage

The company ended the quarter with $142 million of liquidity, excluding the later preferred stock raise. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA was 2.1 times, while net debt represented 19% of total gross assets, supporting management’s description of a conservative capital structure.

Revolving Credit Facility Extension

Following the quarter, the company extended its existing $87.5 million revolving credit facility by 90 days to January 2027. Management said the extension provides more flexibility to evaluate financing alternatives and manage the capital structure.

Expanded Equity Research Coverage

Stifel Nicolaus and Huntington Capital Markets initiated coverage of the company. Their additions brought total equity research coverage to eight firms, potentially increasing visibility among institutional and retail investors.

Cannabis Regulation and Market Developments

The DEA completed its hearing on a proposal to move marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III. Management said reform could improve industry economics and access to traditional capital, but emphasized that the timing and outcome remain uncertain; Florida also approved 22 additional medical cannabis licenses.

Cannabis Sales Milestones

Massachusetts surpassed $10 billion in cumulative adult-use cannabis sales in September. California has generated nearly $8.4 billion in cannabis tax revenue since 2018, underscoring the scale of the markets served by the company’s tenants.

Portfolio Re-Tenanting Progress

The company regained possession of properties previously leased to Parallel, PharmCann and The Cannabis Company. Management said the transitions create new leasing opportunities, with replacement leases already signed for certain properties, including a Battle Green asset in New York and a 4Front property in Washington.

Capital-Efficient Re-Tenanting

Year-to-date re-tenanting costs were well below $10 per square foot. The figure includes commissions, tenant improvements, landlord work and other related expenses, suggesting that the company has so far managed transitions without heavy capital requirements.

Operator Financial Challenges

Financial pressure remains an issue for some cannabis operators, even as established companies pursue expansion and mergers and acquisitions. The uneven financial health of tenants continues to pose a risk to rent collection and property performance.

Federal Reform Remains Uncertain

The proposed federal rescheduling of marijuana still requires additional administrative review. Management cautioned that neither the timing nor the final outcome is certain, limiting the ability to rely on reform as an immediate improvement to tenant economics.

Vacancy Following Tenant Possessions

Remaining vacancy was slightly more than 800,000 square feet. About two-thirds of that space is tied to two Florida properties previously leased to Parallel, making those assets the largest concentration of the company’s current vacant space.

Re-Leasing May Take Time

Management said the process from identifying a new tenant to lease commencement, license transfer and regulatory approval has historically taken six to 18 months. This timeline could delay the return of vacant properties to income-producing status.

Nonrecurring AFFO Benefits

Management said several third-quarter AFFO benefits will not repeat, including items related to PharmCann, Parallel and Bavarian. The company also does not provide forward guidance on AFFO, making the quarterly result an imperfect measure of ongoing earnings power.

Security Deposits Mostly Exhausted

Of five tenants discussed during the call, four had fully used their security deposits. Some deposits remained for a handful of properties associated with The Cannabis Company, but the limited cushion highlights tenant-level financial pressure.

Leasing Agreements Need Approvals

The additional 446,000 square feet covered by agreements remains subject to due diligence, licensing and regulatory approvals. Management stressed that there is no assurance the discussions and negotiations will ultimately result in completed leases.

Terminated Lease Activity

The company discussed 16 terminated leases, most involving cultivation assets. Nearly half of the related square footage came from two Florida properties recovered from Parallel, with other terminations involving PharmCann, Battle Green and 4Front.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management does not provide guidance on whether quarterly AFFO will remain above the $1.90 dividend payout. The Alewife Park loan is expected to be funded through the fourth quarter of 2027 at an average rate of about 15.8%, while life science investments are projected to reach roughly 26% of annualized income; an additional $155 million IQHQ opportunity remains possible, subject to capital decisions.

The earnings call showed a company making measurable progress in AFFO, leasing and portfolio diversification. Strong liquidity and life science growth offer support, but vacancy, tenant stress, regulatory uncertainty and the long re-leasing process remain key issues for investors to monitor.

data.description:
Kkr Reit ((KREF)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

KREF Earnings Call Shows Balance-Sheet Gains Amid Credit Strain

KREF’s earnings call offered a mixed picture. Repayments, liquidity, leverage reduction and progress on legacy assets strengthened the balance sheet, but large quarterly losses, a realized Boston life science loss, refinancing risks and possible higher reserves underscored continuing credit pressure.

Repayments Surpass Full-Year Goal

KREF reported $2.4 billion of repayments year to date, exceeding its $2 billion expectation for the full year. Third-quarter repayments reached $1.2 billion, nearly matching the annual totals recorded in both 2024 and 2025.

Portfolio Rotates Away From Older Loans

More than 80% of year-to-date repayments came from loans originated in 2021 and 2022. Management said this accelerated the portfolio’s natural rotation and reduced exposure to vintages originated during a period of peak valuations.

Progress on Legacy Exposures

KREF said it materially reduced its watchlist, advanced legacy resolutions and addressed its life science portfolio while shifting toward newer loans with stronger credit characteristics. Three additional watchlist loans were resolved during the quarter.

Liquidity Reaches a Historic High

Quarter-end liquidity rose to about $853 million, including $166 million of cash, $53 million of loan repayments held by a servicer and $600 million of undrawn corporate revolver capacity. Management described the position as one of the strongest in KREF’s history and well above its historical average of roughly $600 million.

Leverage Falls Sharply

Strong repayment activity lowered debt-to-equity from 2.6 times to 2.2 times and total leverage from 4.3 times to 3.1 times. Total leverage is now below the company’s historical target range, providing additional balance-sheet flexibility.

CRE CLO Retirement Completed

KREF completed the retirement of its two remaining commercial real estate collateralized loan obligations by exercising optional redemptions. Management said the shrinking collateral pools had made the structures less efficient than other available non-mark-to-market financing options.

New Lending Continues

KREF originated $157 million of loans during the quarter, including a Class A senior housing portfolio secured by four U.S. properties and a Class A Texas office property. Management said credit spreads were relatively stable, financing was readily available and market liquidity remained healthy.

Property Fundamentals Remain Constructive

Management said underlying property fundamentals were generally constructive across most sectors. Tenant demand and a meaningful slowdown in new construction activity continue to support operating conditions, although financing and valuation pressures remain important risks.

KKR Maintains Broad Origination Reach

KKR’s real estate credit team remains active across bank, insurance and debt-fund capital pools. The platform is originating loans across approximately $43 billion of real estate credit assets under management, giving KREF access to a broad lending network.

Lending and Equity Opportunities Expand

Management described lending conditions as attractive because new loans can be made on a reset basis in a higher-rate environment, while supply is declining. KKR remains focused on multifamily and industrial lending, with senior housing also active, and is paying greater attention to value-add and opportunistic multifamily equity investments.

Raleigh Multifamily Asset Improves

KREF said its Raleigh, North Carolina, multifamily asset has been stabilized through stronger cash flow and improved operations. Occupancy and cash flow were described as favorable, suggesting progress at an asset that had previously required closer attention.

Quarterly Losses Weigh on Results

KREF reported a third-quarter 2026 GAAP net loss of $6 million, or $0.11 per share, and a distributable loss of $152 million, or $2.64 per share. Before realized losses and strategic review expenses, distributable earnings were $5 million, or $0.09 per share.

Higher Rates Pressure Borrowers

Management said the recent rise in interest rates has renewed pressure on property values. Borrowers face higher debt-service costs and lower refinancing proceeds, particularly on assets financed at peak valuations in 2021 and early 2022.

Resolutions May Take Longer

KREF expects the current environment to extend resolution timelines and, in some cases, produce additional credit losses. Some transactions once expected to close before year-end are now likely to extend into the first half of 2027.

Reserves Could Rise

Management said difficult liquidity and valuation conditions could lead to higher reserves in the near term as resolutions advance. KREF is marking assets and maintaining current expected credit loss reserves based on market conditions, while acknowledging that some markets remain opaque and illiquid.

Multifamily Refinancing Is a Key Risk

Multifamily loans, particularly from the 2021 and 2022 vintages, are facing pressure from higher rates and lower values. Management said loans at the lower end of the debt-yield range may have the greatest refinancing difficulty, with referenced legacy loans averaging debt yields in the mid-to-high sixes.

Boston Life Science Loan Ends in Loss

KREF assigned its non-recourse Boston life science loan back to the lender after asset values changed. The quarter included a loss on KREF’s portion of the loan, and the asset was removed from the company’s portfolio.

Strategic Review Continues

An independent strategic review committee has retained financial and legal advisers and continues to assess strategic alternatives. Management offered no further details about the process during the call.

Review Expenses Expected to Increase

Strategic review costs primarily consist of financial and legal adviser fees. Management said expenses were back-ended in the third quarter and are expected to increase in the fourth quarter on a full-quarter basis.

Higher Rates Offer Limited Earnings Benefit

KREF said higher rates are not producing a meaningful bottom-line benefit because some asset floors are already near their limits. Floating-rate debt is also broadly matched with floating-rate loans, while real estate-owned assets generate no income and do not benefit from higher rates.

Share Buybacks Effectively Slow

Share buyback activity largely slowed after the strategic review announcement. Management said capital allocation decisions, including repurchases, are among the key matters being considered by the review committee.

Capital Deployment Remains Measured

KREF said it is deploying capital deliberately rather than replacing repayments with new loans on a dollar-for-dollar basis. The company is prioritizing balance-sheet flexibility as it evaluates lending opportunities and works through legacy exposures.

Guidance Points to Caution

Management expects resolution timelines to extend, with some transactions moving into the first half of 2027, and said reserves could increase in the near term. Originations should remain measured, leverage is expected to stay below its historical range in the fourth quarter, and strategic review expenses are set to rise after back-ended third-quarter costs.

KREF enters the next phase with stronger liquidity, lower leverage and a faster exit from older loan vintages. Still, steep quarterly losses, refinancing pressure, potential credit costs and strategic uncertainty leave the company’s recovery dependent on improved property values and successful asset resolutions.

Tpg Re Finance Trust ((TRTX)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

TRTX’s earnings call carried a broadly positive tone, supported by strong origination activity, growing net earning assets, higher net interest income, full portfolio performance, improved financing and ample liquidity. Management also acknowledged pressure from elevated rates, weaker acquisition activity, wider multifamily spreads, higher leverage, a $13 million realized loss and a decline in book value per share.

Strong New Investment Activity

TRTX closed $773 million of new investments in the third quarter and increased net earning assets by $600 million. Since September 2025, the company has originated $2.3 billion of loans, equal to nearly 45% of its current portfolio and helping drive 36% year-over-year growth in net earning assets.

Net Interest Income Accelerates

Net interest income rose about 13% from the second quarter, an increase of roughly $3 million, as the loan portfolio expanded. Management said recent originations should make a larger earnings contribution once they are reflected over a full reporting period.

Credit Performance Remains Resilient

Management reported no meaningful volatility in risk ratings or CECL reserves during the quarter. The loan portfolio was 100% performing at period-end, while its weighted average risk rating held steady at 3.0.

Diversified Portfolio Structure

TRTX held 59 loan investments secured by more than 150 underlying properties, representing $5.2 billion of total commitments. The average loan was $88 million, while multifamily and industrial properties accounted for about 75% of the portfolio.

Balance Sheet Optimization Nears Completion

The company said it has largely completed its balance sheet optimization by diversifying funding, extending liability duration, reducing mark-to-market exposure and improving liquidity. About 75% of leverage is funded through series CRE CLOs and a term loan B, providing more stable, long-duration capital.

FL8 CRE CLO Adds Funding Flexibility

TRTX completed its eighth CRE CLO, securitizing about $1 billion of collateral that was approximately 95% multifamily and industrial. The leverage-neutral transaction generated nearly $43 million in net cash proceeds, is expected to reduce funding costs and lifted non-mark-to-market financing to about 85%.

Reinvestment Capacity Supports Growth

The FL8 transaction created a new 30-month reinvestment period. Combined with existing windows in FL6 and FL7, the structure gives TRTX additional flexibility to recycle capital and support earnings growth.

Share Repurchase Authorization Doubled

TRTX exhausted its previous $25 million repurchase plan, buying 1.2 million shares at a weighted average price of $8 for total consideration of $9.3 million. The purchases increased book value per share by $0.04, and the board approved a new $50 million authorization.

Dividend Covered Before Realized Losses

Distributable earnings before realized losses totaled $18.1 million, or $0.24 per diluted common share. That result covered the common dividend for the quarter, although earnings after the realized loss were materially lower.

Lower Funding Costs and Strong Liquidity

The weighted average cost of funds fell to 1.81% from 1.95% a year earlier. Near-term liquidity was $291.6 million, including cash, undrawn secured capacity, revolver availability and CRE CLO proceeds, while unencumbered loans and total available financing capacity provided additional balance sheet flexibility.

Recent-Vintage Loans Improve Positioning

Management said most of the balance sheet was originated during the past two years and was sized for a higher-rate environment. About 80% of multifamily exposure was originated in 2024 or later, and that share could rise toward 90% after expected repayments.

Strong Pipeline, More Controlled Portfolio Growth

The lending pipeline remains strong, with demand continuing in multifamily and industrial markets. As TRTX moves closer to its target leverage and balance sheet size, management expects activity to become more of a one-in, one-out model, potentially making distributable earnings more stable.

REO Portfolio Remains Earnings Positive

Management said the REO portfolio is contributing positively to quarterly distributable earnings rather than weighing on results. TRTX is in the final stages of marketing one multifamily property and has an LOI in place, with no major change to its monetization strategy.

Rate Floors and Spreads Improve Loan Economics

Loan rate floors have been gradually rising from the former general range of 2.5% to 3%. CRE CLO back-leverage spreads were about 25 basis points wider than when FL8 was launched, a shift that is beginning to support wider loan spreads while TRTX’s liabilities remain locked at tighter levels.

Industrial Fundamentals Stay Resilient

Management described industrial fundamentals as resilient, citing positive leasing momentum across the company’s exposure. Industrial spreads remain relatively firm, although transaction activity has been limited because many assets have already been refinanced or otherwise termed out.

Rental Demand Supports Multifamily

The elevated cost of homeownership and higher borrowing costs continue to make renting more attractive than buying for many households. Management said those conditions are supporting strong demand across the multifamily properties in its portfolio.

Covenants Remain in Compliance

TRTX remained in compliance with all financial covenants at the end of the quarter. The result provides reassurance about the company’s financing structure despite increased leverage and challenging real estate conditions.

Inflation and High Rates Remain Headwinds

Management said inflation has been more persistent than expected, extending the period of elevated interest rates and tight financial conditions. Higher borrowing costs, declining property values in some sectors and heavy refinancing needs continue to pressure real estate owners.

Book Value Declines During Quarter

Book value per common share decreased by $0.10 from June 30 to $10.85 at quarter-end. Management attributed the decline mainly to credit loss expense related to portfolio growth and broader macroeconomic conditions.

Leverage Moves Higher

Total leverage increased to 4.03x from 3.32x at June 30. The rise reflected TRTX’s substantial investment activity during the quarter and underscores the importance of disciplined balance sheet management.

Acquisition Activity Continues to Fade

Management said the gap between buyers and sellers, particularly in multifamily, continues to widen and has pushed acquisition activity lower. New acquisitions remain rare, extending a trend that has persisted for the past two or three years.

Deal Closings Take Longer

The period between signing a transaction and closing has lengthened across the market. Management said these extended timelines can put pressure on earnings and add uncertainty to the timing of portfolio growth.

Multifamily Loan Modified After Vacancy Spike

A multifamily property in a Sunbelt market experienced a sharp increase in vacancy linked to migration trends. TRTX modified the loan to give the property a path toward stabilization and provide the borrower with time to execute a recovery plan.

Multifamily Spreads Widen

Management said spreads on newly built Class A-plus multifamily loans were about 15 to 30 basis points wider. Class B and C real estate, particularly multifamily, saw wider spreads of approximately 25 to 50 basis points.

Selective Lending Limits New Acquisitions

TRTX is seeing very little new acquisition activity and said it is passing on 99% of the office, mixed-use and hotel deals it reviews. The approach reflects a focus on asset quality and disciplined underwriting in a difficult market.

Legacy Loans Face Refinancing Pressure

Loans originated in 2021 and earlier are reaching maturity and may require borrowers to contribute cash equity when refinancing. Management cited an institutional Class A transaction where repaying an agency loan would require a new equity infusion.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management expects recent-vintage multifamily exposure to rise from roughly 80% toward 90% as repayments occur, while higher rate floors and wider market spreads begin to flow into loan economics. The pipeline remains strong, but growth is expected to become more measured through one-in, one-out activity as leverage and balance sheet targets approach; the company also said one multifamily REO is nearing a marketed sale under an existing LOI.

Overall, TRTX delivered strong portfolio growth, improving financing and resilient credit metrics, while maintaining dividend coverage before realized losses.
