data.title: Adaptive Biotechnologies Earnings Call Signals Strong Momentum
data.description:
Adaptive Biotechnologies ((ADPT)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Adaptive Biotechnologies delivered a strongly positive earnings call, highlighted by profitability ahead of expectations, accelerating clinical demand and robust pharmaceutical growth. Higher guidance, expanding margins, a larger backlog and favorable multiple myeloma developments outweighed concerns over Medicare pricing pressure, CMS data issues and uncertain milestone timing.

Profitability Arrived Ahead of Expectations

Adaptive reached total-company profitability earlier than expected in the third quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was positive at $14.3 million, while GAAP net income reached $2.8 million, marking a notable improvement in operating performance.

Revenue Growth and Cash Position Strengthened

Total revenue rose 39% year over year to $83.9 million, supported by MRD growth and revenue from the Pfizer rheumatoid arthritis agreement. Adaptive generated $8 million in free cash flow and ended the quarter with approximately $386 million in total cash.

MRD Revenue Beat Expectations

MRD revenue increased 28% to $72.6 million and represented 86% of company revenue. Excluding $6.5 million of milestone revenue recognized a year earlier, core MRD revenue grew 44%, driven by clinical testing and pharmaceutical sequencing.

Clinical Testing Volume Accelerated

Clinical testing volume climbed 46% year over year, helping clinical revenue grow 41%. Adaptive delivered nearly 40,000 clonoSEQ tests in the quarter, a 10% sequential increase, with every reimbursed indication contributing to the expansion.

DLBCL and Multiple Myeloma Led Volume Growth

DLBCL posted the strongest sequential growth, rising 20%, with gains spread across community and academic accounts. Multiple myeloma represented 45% of clinical volume and increased 11% sequentially, reinforcing its importance to the testing business.

Blood-Based Testing Continued to Expand

Blood-based testing rose 68% year over year and 12% sequentially, reaching 51% of total clonoSEQ volume. In multiple myeloma, blood-based tests accounted for 31% of MRD testing, showing broader adoption of less invasive monitoring.

Community Adoption and EMR Integration Improved

Community volume grew 14% sequentially and represented 37% of total volume, up from 31% a year earlier. Nearly half of orders came from EMR-integrated accounts, while 78% of serial monitoring orders due at Flatiron-integrated community accounts had been fulfilled.

Clinician Reach Expanded

About 5,600 clinicians ordered clonoSEQ in the third quarter, a 37% year-over-year increase. That figure represents roughly 40% of U.S. hematology and oncology providers, indicating continued growth in the test’s clinical reach.

Average Selling Price and Coverage Improved

U.S. average selling price was $1,380, up 3% year over year and roughly flat sequentially. Adaptive expanded commercial coverage in DLBCL and MCL, added Medicaid coverage in Illinois and Ohio, and established coverage in states representing about 62% of Medicaid testing volume.

Longer-Term Pricing Opportunity Remained

Management continued to target an average selling price of approximately $1,400 for the full year. Its longer-term goal is $1,700 to $1,800 per test, supported by broader coverage, more frequent testing and a proposed maintenance-testing bundle.

Maintenance Testing Bundle Went to MolDX

Adaptive submitted a technical assessment to MolDX for an additional multiple myeloma maintenance-testing bundle and said discussions were active. The proposal covers five additional tests during maintenance, although the final number of tests and timing remain uncertain.

Updated Guidelines Strengthened clonoSEQ’s Position

Updated NCCN guidelines gave MRD testing greater prominence, specifically named clonoSEQ and preferred an FDA-approved assay with 10^-6 sensitivity. The guidelines also identified testing points during maintenance and surveillance and said MRD results can inform treatment decisions and monitoring.

New Cure Definition Supported Repeated Testing

The International Myeloma Working Group’s new cure definition calls for five years off treatment with sustained MRD negativity, demonstrated by at least four negative assessments. Management said clonoSEQ aligns with the requirements, supporting its role in recurrence monitoring.

Pharma Sequencing Growth Remained Strong

Underlying MRD pharmaceutical sequencing revenue grew 55% year over year when milestones were excluded. Adaptive added 27 new or amended studies, bringing its active global portfolio to 191 studies and underscoring the expanding use of MRD in drug development.

Pharma Backlog Increased Significantly

MRD pharmaceutical backlog reached approximately $270 million, up 34% from $200 million a year earlier. Multiple myeloma represented about 60% of active studies, 65% of backlog and 79% of new bookings during the quarter.

MRD Adoption in Drug Development Expanded

Nineteen multiple myeloma studies now use MRD as a primary endpoint, compared with 12 a year ago. clonoSEQ was used in 23 interventional studies across multiple myeloma, CLL and ALL, while additional testing points and MRD-guided designs increased bookings per study.

Margins and Operating Leverage Improved

Total company gross margin was 76%, while sequencing gross margin increased to 73% from 66% a year earlier. Lab efficiencies after the NovaSeq X transition and higher testing volumes helped lift MRD adjusted EBITDA to $15.1 million from $7 million.

Immune Medicine Separation Progressed

Adaptive said it was working with Morgan Stanley on the separation of its Immune Medicine business. Management remained on track to announce the path forward by year-end, making the separation an important strategic development for investors.

Pfizer Milestone Was Earned

The Immune Medicine business earned a milestone payment from Pfizer after successfully delivering rheumatoid arthritis data under its agreement. Immune Medicine revenue was $11.3 million, primarily from the Pfizer target-discovery deal, while adjusted EBITDA was $3.2 million.

DLBCL Competitive Position Stayed Strong

Management acknowledged competitive noise in DLBCL but expressed confidence in clonoSEQ’s position. It pointed to technology built for blood cancers, established reimbursement, real-world experience involving approximately 9,000 patients and long-standing customer relationships.

GAAP Profitability May Not Persist

Despite third-quarter GAAP net income of $2.8 million, management said it does not currently expect GAAP net income or positive earnings per share in the fourth quarter or for the full year. The comments introduced caution around the durability of the quarter’s profitability.

Medicare Episode Structure Pressured ASP

The Medicare episode rate covers up to four tests over a patient’s lifetime. As physicians monitor patients more frequently, a growing number move beyond that limit, pressuring realized average selling prices, particularly in multiple myeloma.

CMS Preliminary Pricing Data Was Erroneous

Adaptive identified incorrect data submitted to CMS for the clonoSEQ PLA code during the preliminary 2027 rate-setting process. The company said it was working with CMS to correct the information before finalized rates take effect.

Medicaid Remained the Lowest-Paying Segment

Medicaid accounted for about 10% of Adaptive’s payer mix and remained its lowest-paying segment. Even so, Medicaid average selling price increased 26% year over year as coverage expanded across additional states.

Milestone Timing Remained Difficult to Predict

Management said it had no visibility into MRD milestones for the fourth quarter. Milestone timing depends on customers and is difficult to model, although Adaptive reported a healthy pipeline of milestone opportunities over the coming years.

Pharma Revenue Could Remain Lumpy

Adaptive cautioned that pharmaceutical revenue can vary significantly from quarter to quarter because of milestone timing and study activity. The company nevertheless highlighted its growing backlog and expanding study base as important sources of longer-term visibility.

2027 Guidance Was Not Provided

Management did not issue formal guidance for 2027. It said the business is positioned for strong growth in 2027 and beyond, while investors will need to wait for more specific targets and assumptions.

Forward-Looking Guidance

For full-year 2026, Adaptive raised MRD revenue guidance to $276 million-$286 million, including $9 million of milestone revenue, with no further milestones assumed. The midpoint implies 32% MRD growth, or 41% excluding milestones, while clinical volume growth is expected at about 42% and pharma sequencing growth at roughly 25%.

Operating expenses are expected to be approximately $350 million, near the low end of the prior range and about 5% above last year. Adaptive continues to target a full-year average selling price of roughly $1,400 and a longer-term $1,700-$1,800 range, but does not expect GAAP net income or positive EPS in the fourth quarter or full year.

Adaptive Biotechnologies’ quarter showed powerful operating momentum, with profitability, clinical demand, pharma bookings and margins all improving. While reimbursement pressure, pricing uncertainty and uneven milestones remain risks, the raised 2026 outlook and expanding clonoSEQ adoption provided a constructive message for investors.
